newsitem.title: CHINA: China province hit by worst drought since 1949.
newsitem.headline: China province hit by worst drought since 1949.

text.p: The most severe drought in more than four decades has hit China's northern province of Hebei, affecting over half the region's farmland, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
Unusually high temperatures and the lowest reported rainfall in Hebei's history had damaged more than 3.33 million hectares of farmland in the province since June, it said.
There would be no harvest from 200,000 hectares of farmland this year and a further 200,000 hectares had been left unsowable, it said.
The province's water table had dropped 1.28 metres since spring and many wells had dried up, Xinhua said.
Provincial authorities had invested 9.0 million yuan ($1.1 million) in fighting the drought and had sent more than 100,000 agricultural experts to rural areas, it said.

Officials have said drought in northern areas will affect this year's corn crop but the weather is not expected to cut the overall grain harvest below forecast levels of about 484 million tonnes for the year.
